newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland and Russia's Tatarstan seek closer ties.
newsitem.headline: Poland and Russia's Tatarstan seek closer ties.

text.p: Poland and the autonomous Russian republic of Tatarstan on Monday signed a framework agreement under which the two counties aim to boost economic ties and create cultural and student exchanges.

"The agreement is a framework understanding which will be filled by specific settlements (at a future time)," Leszek Miller, the chief of staff in the Polish cabinet, told reporters after the signing ceremony.
Mintimer Shaimiyev, president of oil-rich Tatarstan, said his country was interested in Polish light industry and machinery, perfumes and pharmaceuticals.
"Our goal is to rebuild old contacts (with Poland) but to build them in a new environment of the market economy," Shaimiyev said.

Last year Poland was the forth largest trading partner of Tatarstan, with turnover topping $67 million, according to Rzeczpospolita daily. The Central Asian republic exports mainly oil and oil products to Poland.
